title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification) we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents using gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model-generation calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We present the preregistration, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, an evidence-grounded explanation of the ceiling outcome, and concrete preregisterable design alternatives that would permit detecting verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.

sections.introduction: Translating high-level operator intents into device-level network configurations using large language models (LLMs) promises to accelerate NetOps workflows but creates safety risks when generated configurations violate reachability, access-control, ordering, or workflow invariants. A standard mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that combines stochastic generation with deterministic verification and optional repair or human review. This study asks a narrowly scoped, preregistered question: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? The design isolates verifier detection from generator-side resampling or repair by adopting shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation shared across paired conditions). We executed the preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on 72 preregistered paired intents. The run completed without technical failures and produced a degenerate confirmatory outcome: no baseline emulator faults and a paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0], exact McNemar p = 1.0). Rather than treating this as a mere null result, we analyze why it occurred given the preregistered contract and archived artifacts and provide artifact-grounded guidance for follow-on confirmatory designs able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.
sections.related_work: Prior work shows that LLMs can produce device-level configurations from natural-language intent in constrained vendor-dialect settings and curated evaluations, motivating intent→config automation while noting safety limitations [1]. System and prototype work has proposed multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks that integrate verifiers and domain services into agentic NetOps workflows; these illustrate feasible integration points but typically report emulated or prototype evaluations rather than preregistered paired detector measurements [2]. The generate–verify–repair pattern is well studied in code and software-repair domains where deterministic checkers can convert stochastic generation into correctness-convergent workflows; empirical utility there depends on baseline generator error rates and whether the workflow permits verifier-triggered repair or resampling [3]. Canonical deterministic network-verification techniques (header-space and related reachability/policy analyzers) provide semantics-aware invariants appropriate for the verify stage, but prior literature (as represented in the verified records used here) lacks a preregistered paired experiment that measures how often such verifiers detect faults that would otherwise manifest at execution time [4]. Our study situates itself at this intersection by measuring verifier detection under a shared-candidate paired contract and by archiving per-episode validator traces, generation responses, and deterministic execution accounting for reproducible diagnosis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) defined the primary estimand as the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) under a confirmatory paired design. Target effect and sample: absolute paired reduction 0.20, two-sided α = 0.05, power ≥ 0.80; preregistered N = 72 pairs (24 per stratified difficulty level). Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract. For each intent the adapter requested exactly one initial LLM generation that was shared unchanged across two paired conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record whether an emulator-observed operational fault occurs. Guarded: run the deterministic verifier on the identical candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no executed fault); if not flagged, execute the same candidate in the emulator and record the result. This contract isolates verifier detection from generator-side resampling, prompt engineering, or iterative repair. Models, verifier, and recorded parameters. The declared model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Recorded key fields include declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, and temperature = null. The recorded temperature = null indicates provider-default sampling semantics rather than an explicit numeric temperature; this is an archived sampling-parameter uncertainty. The verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 configured to run the full_intent_constraint_validation rule set and to emit structured validator_traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after snapshots, violation_count, difficulty metadata). Task-generation, contamination, and stratification. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by a task generator that encodes intent, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty.level. Exact-match contamination checks against a public-corpus fingerprint were preregistered; no confirmatory pairs were excluded. Execution accounting and retries. The missingness_plan permitted up to two additional retries for transient hosted-API errors; all retries and provider events were logged. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72. Scoring and inferential scripts. The primary analysis used a deterministic paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor that constructs a 2×2 contingency table (guarded × baseline) where undetected executed fault = 1. The pre-specified inferential test is an exact McNemar two-sided when discordant pairs exist; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) were computed for the paired difference and for verifier detection diagnostics. All analysis scripts and artifacts are archived.

sections.discussion: Interpretation of the degenerate confirmatory outcome. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate estimand validly isolates verifier detection on identical candidates; algebraically, when identical generated candidates produce zero baseline emulator faults the paired difference must be zero and no detector can demonstrate reduction of executed faults. The observed ceiling (n_11 = 72; paired difference = 0.0; CI [0.0,0.0]; p = 1.0) therefore reflects an expected consequence of the combination of (i) constrained task manifests that encoded explicit required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields, (ii) a model run (gpt-5-mini) that produced candidates matching those manifests, and (iii) a verifier rule set (full_intent_constraint_validation) that enforces the same manifest constraints — all of which are measurable in archived validator_traces and task manifests. Design implications and preregisterable alternatives. For confirmatory measurements that can detect verifier utility, the task bank and contract must permit a non-negligible baseline error prevalence or allow the verifier to influence candidate distributions. Concrete, preregisterable alternatives (implementable using the same deterministic infrastructure and archival conventions) include: (A) independent-generation arm: request separate initial generations per condition so that verifier-triggered repair or blocking changes the distribution of executed candidates and the estimand measures net operational improvement; (B) repair-enabled flows: permit one verifier-triggered repair call and execute the repaired candidate to measure end-to-end improvement; (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks: seed tasks with ambiguous wording, vendor-edge cases, or ordering subtleties to increase baseline faults; (D) sampling-parameter sweeps and multi-model comparisons to quantify sampling and model sensitivity (explicit non-null temperature values are required to interpret sampling effects); and (E) cost arms to quantify blocking false-positive costs when the verifier flags but the emulator would have executed without fault. Each alternative changes the estimand or the causal pathway in a preregisterable way and can be power-calculated using the archived analysis utilities. Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates detector effect but prevents measuring verifier-mediated resampling or repair impacts. Construct validity: emulator-executed faults are a conservative surrogate for operational harm and do not capture traffic-dependent failure modes or vendor-hardware idiosyncrasies. External validity: single-model scope (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic/emulated tasks limit generalization to other models and production deployments. Conclusion-readiness: measuring verifier utility in practice requires preregistered designs aligned to expected baseline prevalence and to the operational costs of verifier blocking and repair.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired evaluation under shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate confirmatory outcome: identical LLM-generated candidates (gpt-5-mini) produced no emulator-observed faults on the preregistered task bank and the canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) did not change executed outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This result is internally consistent with the preregistered estimand: a verifier cannot reduce executed faults when none occur for the identical candidate. The archived artifacts (task manifests, generation responses, per-episode validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs) provide a reproducible template and concrete diagnostics. Follow-on preregistered designs that permit independent generation, verifier-triggered repair, adversarial seeding, or multi-model/sampling sweeps are required to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes and to quantify verifier true-positive detection and false-positive blocking costs.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. Human role: a Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and orchestration: initial generation used gpt-5-mini orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before outcome observation. Immutable master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Artifacts and reproducibility: execution and analysis artifacts (generation responses, per-episode validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs) are archived under the study evidence bundle referenced in the paper; those artifacts provide the machine-verifiable provenance for reported numbers. Sampling-parameter note: recorded temperature = null in the archived model configuration indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics rather than an explicit numeric temperature. No human manual manuscript editing occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: the baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit under the shared_initial_candidate contract.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per-condition generation, multi-sample generation, or verifier-triggered repair unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single-model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.
Sampling-parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (provider-default sampling semantics); this is a recorded uncertainty in sampling behavior.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private training-data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
